subject: health
essentialQuestion: How do I speak up for myself, respect others, and repair a relationship after conflict?

prompts.prompt: Explain assertive, respectful communication in your own words and give or identify a valid example.

Use a diagram of a general figure or character rather than your own body, a picture sequence, a model, a described demonstration, or a checked source, to show what you learned about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests.
Apply what you learned about listening and perspective-taking to a new fictional situation. Show the steps or name the source you relied on.
A made-up character makes an unsafe or unreliable choice involving conflict resolution and repair. Explain what is wrong, correct it, and say why the correction is safer.
Connect assertive, respectful communication with inclusion and respect for differences. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write and rehearse assertive communication and conflict-repair scripts for fictional situations, including a bystander response plan.
Name one skill you can now use somewhere else, one way to check your own work, and one question you still have. This is about the skill, not about your private life; nothing private has to be shared.
